set.beta: From the notch at the top of the Barrier, just south of the summit, the route follows Degenhardt's south ridge north to the top. The ground immediately above the notch is the worst of it: unstable boulders and broken rock sitting on steep dirt, climbed to reach the ridge crest. A short steep step on the crest is avoided by a ledge system that traverses left onto the west side of the ridge and leads to easier scrambling; close to the summit the ridge steepens again into a few short, exposed steps past small gendarmes. Most of the climbing is 4th class with a few moves of low 5th, but the rock is loose enough that parties commonly rope up for much of it. Route-finding is the real difficulty: the line is ambiguous when seen from the south, and traversing too low on the west side puts a party on roped ground of about 5.7.
set.approach: Start at the Goodell Creek Trailhead (Goodell Creek Group Camp, ~500-600 ft) off SR-20 just west of Newhalem. The first stretch follows an old logging-road grade/climbers' path along Goodell Creek for a little over a mile before it narrows to a boot-beaten track. Roughly 4 miles in, near Terror Creek, watch for the unmarked junction where the Terror Creek climbers' path splits off — historically flagged only by a rock arrow, a post, and a large cairn, so route-finding here is a genuine crux; the path is well-defined at first but dies out into creek-bottom brush and devils club lower down. Ford/cross Terror Creek at about 2000 ft: the customary crossing is a large log roughly 500 ft upstream of where the path hits the creek, but in high water this log is sometimes submerged and parties have had to scout alternate logs — treat this as a conditions-dependent obstacle, not a given. From the creek, the path grinds directly and relentlessly up the opposing hillside, gaining close to 4000 ft in under two miles through forest, then open heather slopes above treeline — steep and loose in spots. The climbers' path eventually merges into 'Stump Hollow' and follows the narrow crest north to the standard basecamp area near 'Chopping Block Camp' (~6000-6400 ft), the usual base for Southern Pickets objectives. The south ridge starts at the notch at the top of the Barrier — the long rocky rib dividing Terror Basin from Crescent Creek Basin — immediately south of Degenhardt's summit, and it can be reached from either basin. From Terror Basin, climb the Terror Glacier to its upper end (open crevasses can usually be walked around; crampons and an axe are standard here even in summer), then broken rock, heather benches and steep, loose dirt to the notch. From Crescent Creek Basin — reached by traversing Stump Hollow to the roughly 6400 ft saddle near the Chopping Block and descending about 200 ft — a snow ramp rises to the same notch. Parties moving between the two basins cross the Barrier either low, over loose ledges at the base of the Terror Glacier, or high, over moats and steep choss near the top of the glacier just below Degenhardt; both are loose, exposed, and consistently described as 'Pickets Class 3' — sustained, serious, low-fifth-class-feeling terrain despite the modest rating. Total trip is roughly 18.7 miles round-trip with about 600-8100+ ft of elevation range; water is available at Goodell Creek and the Terror Creek crossing, with seasonal snowmelt/tarns higher up that can dry out late season.
set.descent_text: Descend the south ridge. Rappel stations are in place where the ridge steepens near the summit, and a single 55 m rope is enough for them; the slings on the stations are old, so inspect them and back up or replace them if you carry spare cord. Because the rock is loose, most parties that roped on the way up keep the rope out for the upper ridge on the way down. Back at the notch at the top of the Barrier, either take the snow ramp down into Crescent Creek Basin, or reverse the loose ground and the Terror Glacier into Terror Basin (crampons still recommended), then return to camp. The Barrier ground is the main hazard on this leg: loose rock and exposed ledges/choss, more dangerous late in the day when fatigued or in poor light. The next day, reverse the full approach — steep descent off the ridge/Stump Hollow crest to the Terror Creek crossing (re-check the log crossing, since water levels and log position can change), then the climbers' path and Goodell Creek Trail back to the trailhead.
set.rappels: Several rappels from fixed stations on the upper south ridge; a single 55 m rope is enough. The slings on the stations are old — check them and replace as needed.

pitch_detail.notes: The climb starts at the notch at the top of the Barrier, immediately south of the summit. From Terror Basin, go to the top of the Terror Glacier, walking around any open slots, then up broken rock and heather benches to the notch; from Crescent Creek Basin, a snow ramp leads up to the same notch.

From the notch, climb to the crest of the south ridge over unstable boulders and broken rock bedded in steep dirt. This is the chossiest ground on the route: keep the party close together and out of each other's fall line, and expect to want a rope even though the moves are not hard.

A short steep section on the crest is passed by a ledge system traversing left onto the west side of the ridge, which leads to easier scrambling above. This is where parties go wrong: the line is hard to read from below, and traversing too low on the west side leads onto roped climbing of about 5.7 instead of the 4th class ground higher up.

Near the top the ridge steepens into a few short, exposed steps and crosses small gendarmes before the summit. The climbing is mostly 4th class with a few moves of low 5th; the rock stays loose, so most parties belay these steps. Rappel stations for the descent are found along this upper section.

climbing_route.label: Loose ground from the Barrier notch to the ridge crest
climbing_route.notes: From the notch at the top of the Barrier, immediately south of the summit, climb unstable boulders and broken rock bedded in steep dirt to the crest of the south ridge. This is the poorest rock on the route; stay tight as a party and out of each other's fall line.

climbing_route.label: South ridge and the west-side ledges
climbing_route.notes: Follow the ridge north. A short steep step on the crest is turned by a ledge system traversing left onto the west side, leading to easier scrambling. The line is ambiguous: traversing too low on the west side lands a party on roped 5.7 ground rather than the 4th class terrain above it.

climbing_route.label: Summit steps
climbing_route.notes: Close to the summit the ridge steepens into a few short, exposed steps past small gendarmes — 4th class with a few low-5th moves on loose rock. Rappel stations along this section serve the descent. Degenhardt is widely regarded as the chossiest peak in the Southern Pickets, so helmets and careful rope management matter more than the grade suggests.

review.climb: The South Route / South Ridge: from the notch at the top of the Barrier just south of the summit, north up the south ridge to the top. The name 'Southwest Route' matches no documented line. Of the two climbs mixed into the row, the South Route is the better documented (three independent trip reports: a 2006 'S Ridge' report with the full sequence and rap stations, a 'Degenhardt South Route' report with the too-low 5.7 trap and the snow-ramp descent into Crescent Creek Basin, and a 2014 traverse report reaching the notch south of the peak and calling the summit 4th class), and it already owns the climbing_route, pitch_detail entries 2-3 (traversing too low; the 5.7 step), the low-5th grade and the rappel column. The Corkscrew Route (Class 4 slot to the north ridge, Class 4-5 face to the west ridge, Class 3 ledge to the south ridge) rests on a single trip report and survives only in descent_text and the generic 'Crescent Creek Basin to the summit horn' wording, so it was removed rather than chosen. A Crescent Creek Basin start still fits the South Route, because a snow ramp connects that basin to the same notch.
review.changed: beta rewritten for the south ridge (was a generic Crescent Creek 'southwest slope to the summit horn' line). approach: kept verbatim through Chopping Block Camp; replaced the final Degenhardt leg (which ended at 'the base of the southwest line') with the two documented ways to the Barrier notch; kept the Barrier-crossing and trip-total sentences; dropped the testimony parenthetical about a climber tearing a calf muscle. descent_text: removed the corkscrew downclimb, the single 30-40 ft rappel off a horn, the 30 m rope claim, the 'no bolts' claim and the 3.5-4 h summit-to-camp time (all corkscrew-report facts); now describes rappelling the south ridge on fixed stations with a 55 m rope and descending from the notch into either basin; kept the Barrier hazard and hike-out sentences. rappels rewritten (several stations, 55 m rope, old slings) instead of 'single-rope rappel from summit anchors'. pitch_detail: 4 -> 4 entries; kept labels Approach, Lower wall, Summit ridge; renamed 'Crux step' to 'West-side ledge traverse' and removed its '5.4-5.7' grade and the crux implication, because no source assigns a grade to that section (the 5.7 is the off-route too-low line, stated in notes). No lengths, bolt counts or per-section grades added; all four are now travel stages with terrain chips. climbing_route replaced: removed the tower-at-the-final-notch, the south-side rappel anchor and the meltwater-on-slabs material, which come from a report of the Northwest route from the Terror-Degenhardt col, not the south ridge. overview and fa left as they are (peak-level facts).
review.duplicate_check: No other Degenhardt row found. show.mjs only reads by id, so these ids were tried and do not exist: wa_mount_degenhardt_south_route, wa_degenhardt_south_route, wa_south_route, wa_mount_degenhardt_south_ridge, wa_mount_degenhardt_south_face, wa_mount_degenhardt_southwest_face, wa_mount_degenhardt_west_ridge, wa_mount_degenhardt_north_ridge, wa_mount_degenhardt_corkscrew_route, wa_corkscrew_route, wa_mount_degenhardt_standard_route, wa_mount_degenhardt_standard, wa_mount_degenhardt_normal_route, wa_mount_degenhardt_south_side, wa_degenhardt_southwest_route. OPEN QUESTION for the applier: list every route with area_id = 'wa_mount_degenhardt' before renaming, since a row with a non-obvious id could not be ruled out.

name.evidence: Trip reports call this line 'Degenhardt South Route' and 'S Ridge Degenhardt'. No source uses 'Southwest Route'. 'South Ridge' would also be accurate; 'South Route' is the name used by the report that documents the too-low 5.7 trap.

grade.evidence: Stored 'Grade III, 5.6' is unsourced. Reports: roped climbing 'mostly 4th class with a few spots of low 5th' (2006); '4th class summit' (2014); 'low fifth-class' overall with 5.7 only when a party traversed too low. No commitment grade (II/III) is stated in any source, so none is proposed.

discipline.evidence: Glacier/snow approach plus roped loose 4th/low-5th ridge.

review.other_findings: Mount Degenhardt has at least three documented lines: this South Route (south ridge from the Barrier notch), a Northwest route from near the Terror-Degenhardt col via a northern gully (2015 and 2025 reports; the 2015 party descended with two rappels), and the Corkscrew Route from Crescent Creek Basin (single report). If the owner wants the Corkscrew or the Northwest route in the catalog, it would be a new row, not this one.
review.applied_note: Before applying, the descriptive 'grade' values (e.g. 'Loose boulders, steep dirt') were removed from pitch_detail: that key renders as a grade and no source gives per-section grades; the notes carry the difficulty.

wa_robinson_mountain_north_couloir.skip_reason: UNDOCUMENTED — recommend deletion. No description of a north couloir on Robinson Mountain exists in any source found; the documented lines are the Southeast Ridge (already its own row, wa_robinson_mountain_southeast_ridge) and a steep couloir on the EAST face that has been skied.

review.climb: None identifiable. Not a DUPLICATE of wa_robinson_mountain_southeast_ridge (its pitch table describes a snow couloir, not the ridge), and not the east-face couloir either (its approach, aspect and descent do not describe that line).
review.searched: Web searches for 'Robinson Mountain' with north couloir / north face / north side / N couloir / NW couloir / north gully, ski and couloir terms, Devils Peak saddle, Methow and Mazama ski terms; site searches of cascadeclimbers.com (only SE Ridge reports: 2007, 2014, 2023) and peakbagger.com. Pages read: SummitPost Robinson Mountain (archived copy; routes and trip-report list all SE ridge / Beauty Creek), Where is Kyle Miller (east-face couloir only, mid-40s degrees, ~2000 ft ski descent), Lemke Climbs (SE ridge only), both Brisbine Robinson reports (SE ridge only), Turns All Year 'Spell of the Pasayten' 2018 (east cirque/east flank skied), Wikipedia (SE ridge standard; ridges run west, north and southeast). The Mountaineers route page, NWHikers thread and peakbagger peak page were blocked (403/JS wall) and could not be read.
review.other_findings: The stored text looks fabricated rather than mis-filed: (1) its beta's register claim ('a 2005 party found no register entries suggesting an ascent since 2003') distorts a Southeast Ridge report, which says a register placed in 2002 had its second entry of 2005 a week after the first; (2) its approach sends parties to the Robinson-Devils Peak saddle and then 'east' under the north face, but Devils Peak lies about 1.9 miles east-southeast of Robinson, so that traverse cannot reach a north face; (3) the pitch lengths (91 m / 305 m / 30 m) and 40-50 degree grade have no source. No corrections written, per brief.
